verses.zh: （ 可 拉 後 裔 的 詩 歌 ， 交 與 伶 長 。 調 用 女 音 。 ） 神 是 我 們 的 避 難 所 ， 是 我 們 的 力 量 ， 是 我 們 在 患 難 中 隨 時 的 幫 助 。
verses.en: For the music director, by the Korahites; according to the alamoth style;[NOTE:1] a song.God is our strong refuge;[NOTE:2] he is truly our helper in times of trouble.[NOTE:3]
notes: Psalm 46. In this so-called “Song Of Zion” God’s people confidently affirm that they are secure because the great warrior-king dwells within Jerusalem and protects it from the nations that cause such chaos in the earth. A refrain (vv. 7, 11) concludes the song’s two major sections.
The meaning of the Hebrew term עֲלָמוֹת (‘alamot, alamoth, which means “young women”) is uncertain; perhaps it refers to a particular style of music. Cf. 1 Chr 15:20.
Heb “our refuge and strength,” which is probably a hendiadys meaning “our strong refuge” (see Ps 71:7). Another option is to translate, “our refuge and source of strength.”

verses.en: For this reason we do not fear[NOTE:1] when the earth shakes,[NOTE:2] and the mountains tumble into the depths of the sea,[NOTE:3]

verses.zh: 你 們 來 看 耶 和 華 的 作 為 ， 看 他 使 地 怎 樣 荒 涼 。
verses.en: Come, Witness the exploits[NOTE:1] of the Lord,who brings devastation to the earth.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 46. In this so-called “Song Of Zion” God’s people confidently affirm that they are secure because the great warrior-king dwells within Jerusalem and protects it from the nations that cause such chaos in the earth. A refrain (vv. 7, 11) concludes the song’s two major sections.

verses.zh: 他 止 息 刀 兵 ， 直 到 地 極 ； 他 折 弓 、 斷 槍 ， 把 戰 車 焚 燒 在 火 中 。
verses.en: He brings an end to wars throughout the earth.[NOTE:1] He shatters[NOTE:2] the bow and breaks[NOTE:3] the spear;he burns[NOTE:4] the shields with fire.[NOTE:5]
notes: Psalm 46. In this so-called “Song Of Zion” God’s people confidently affirm that they are secure because the great warrior-king dwells within Jerusalem and protects it from the nations that cause such chaos in the earth. A refrain (vv. 7, 11) concludes the song’s two major sections.

Heb “our refuge and strength,” which is probably a hendiadys meaning “our strong refuge” (see Ps 71:7). Another option is to translate, “our refuge and source of strength.”
Heb “a helper in times of trouble he is found [to be] greatly.” The perfect verbal form has a generalizing function here. The adverb מְאֹד (meʾod, “greatly”) has an emphasizing function.

The imperfect is taken in a generalizing sense (cf. NEB) because the situation described in vv. 2-3 is understood as symbolizing typical world conditions. In this case the imperfect draws attention to the typical nature of the response. The covenant community characteristically responds with confidence, not fear. Another option is to take the situation described as purely hypothetical. In this case one might translate, “We will not fear, even though the earth should shake” (cf. NIV, NRSV).

verses.en: He says,[NOTE:1] “Stop your striving and recognize[NOTE:2] that I am God.I will be exalted[NOTE:3] over[NOTE:4] the nations! I will be exalted over[NOTE:5] the earth!”
